article_notes: Prospective cohort of 320 dogs with PCR/RLB-confirmed B. rossi mono-infection (Onderstepoort, 2006-2016), pooled from 3 data bases; two of the cohorts have been published elsewhere (Schoeman, Goddard, Koster, Dvir, Rees et al.), so these dogs overlap with other articles. All samples were taken before treatment. Outcome = short-term survival to discharge vs death/euthanasia (34 died, 10.6%; all within 24 h of admission). Most group comparisons (died vs survived; collapsed vs able to stand) are reported in text only, with the medians in supplementary Table S1, which is not in the Markdown. A multivariable logistic regression found no set of independent predictors of death, so only univariable ORs are reported (no multivariable rows). Joint correspondence analysis (Figure 2) clustered death with collapse, high urea, bilirubin and cortisol, low temperature and low T4; not extracted as rows (no statistic). Inconsistencies between text and tables: band cell OR 5.9 (text) vs 4.9 (Table 1); urea '>20 mmol/L' OR 30.95 in text is the % died in Table 1 (OR 9.1); bilirubin sensitivity/specificity 75/81.6 in text vs 87.5/76.3 in Table 3; Table 1 cerebral-signs row prints 321 dogs without cerebral signs; Table 1 '% that died' for collapse (14, 24) is inconsistent with the text. Table values were used. S3 (degree of anaemia, Hct as a continuous measure) was added for correlations of markers with Hct, following the guide; these rows are weaker evidence of a severity association. Platelet count, urine SG, PaO2 <60 mmHg mortality and post-mortem findings were not compared between outcome groups and were not extracted. No healthy control group.

severity_definitions.label: died vs survived
severity_definitions.definition: Short-term outcome: survival to discharge vs death or euthanasia due to poor prognosis. 34 of 320 dogs died; all deaths within 24 h of admission.
severity_definitions.quote: Outcome was recorded as short-term survival (i.e. until discharge), or death/euthanasia due to poor prognosis.

severity_definitions.label: collapsed vs able to stand (non-collapsed)
severity_definitions.definition: Collapse at presentation, defined as unable to stand unaided, as a marker of clinical severity at admission.
severity_definitions.quote: Seventy-two of the 320 cases (22.5%) were collapsed at presentation (unable to stand unaided).

severity_definitions.label: degree of anaemia (haematocrit)
severity_definitions.definition: Severity of anaemia measured by admission haematocrit, used as a continuous measure for correlations and the ISA comparison. The authors also grade anaemia as severe (Hct <0.15 L/L), moderate (0.15-0.24), mild (0.25-0.36).
severity_definitions.quote: Of the dogs that had haematocrit (Hct) determined at admission, 113 (35.6%) were classified as severely anaemic (Hct<0.15%L/L) with a mortality of 14.2%, 81 (25.5%) were moderately anaemic (Hct 0.15 – 0.24 L/L) with a mortality of 8%

associations.quote: There was a strong inverse correlation between Hct and absolute reticulocyte count in the 113 cases in which the absolute reticulocyte count was determined (p<0.01, correlation coefficient - 0.312).
associations.note: Inverse correlation with Hct, so more reticulocytes with more severe anaemia (positive_association with anaemia severity). Spearman per Methods.
